title: Credit Department Basis — Energy Invoices, Arrears Charges and Delivery Holds
content:
This basis governs invoices raised on Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts and what follows when they are not paid.

**When an invoice falls due.** The clause formerly stated here — "An energy invoice falls due the programme's terms in calendar days after the invoice date, a payment landing on the due date itself still being on time." — is carried for the record and is no longer in force as the basis on which the amount standing falls due.

**Late charge and service charge.** The clause formerly stated here — "An invoice still unpaid after the programme's grace period, counted in whole calendar days from the due date, carries the programme's late charge once and then the programme's monthly service charge for as long as it stands unpaid." — is carried for the record and is no longer in force as the basis on which those charges are arrived at. For the record, the grace period under that clause ran from the due date as its anchor, was counted in whole calendar days, was taken from the programme's grace period figure in the catalogue, and was read as a not-earlier-than test whose boundary was exclusive: a day landing exactly on the end of the grace period was not yet beyond it, and the evidence for it was the invoice reference, its date and the amount standing as the system carried them, never the member's account of when the bill arrived.

**Past due and delivery holds.** The account is flagged past due from the first day an invoice is overdue, and further deliveries are held once the oldest overdue invoice reaches the programme's delivery hold in days; the hold stops fuel going out and does not stop the budget plan being billed.

**How payments reach the cooperative and where they land.** Payments may reach the cooperative only by the methods the programme allows and are applied oldest invoice first unless the member names an invoice.

**Grain proceeds.** Where a member has elected to have grain settlement proceeds credited to the energy account and the programme allows the transfer, the whole net of that settlement lands as one payment on the settlement date.

**Lifting a hold.** A delivery hold is lifted only when the overdue balance is cleared; the cooperative makes an exception for a tank that is out of fuel in freezing weather, which is a safety judgement for the energy manager and not a matter this rule settles.

## Two questions the desk is asked

**A payment arrives naming no invoice. Where does it go?** Oldest invoice first. The member may direct it otherwise by naming an invoice.

**Does a delivery hold stop the level instalments being billed?** No. The hold stops fuel going out; the instalments continue to be billed.

superseded_clauses: An energy invoice falls due the programme's terms in calendar days after the invoice date, a payment landing on the due date itself still being on time.

An invoice still unpaid after the programme's grace period, counted in whole calendar days from the due date, carries the programme's late charge once and then the programme's monthly service charge for as long as it stands unpaid.
